point1_synthesis: Markets this week are being driven by one interlocking story: a hotter-than-expected core CPI print (+0.3% m/m) pushed the market-implied odds of a Fed rate hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC from roughly 70% to 90%, sending the 10-year Treasury yield up 12bp to 4.95% — its highest level since 2023 and closing in on 2007 highs. Middle East tensions, including Iran's attacks on commercial and U.S. Navy vessels, are compounding the inflation picture by pushing WTI crude up 3.2% to $97. Credit markets aren't stressed — both IG and HY spreads tightened slightly on the week — and the VIX term structure remains in contango, meaning options markets aren't pricing panic despite small-caps (Russell 2000, -2.2% over 5 days) and the Dow (-2.1%) underperforming a Nasdaq held up by AI-infrastructure capex names. The FOMC decision on Sept 16 is the next clear catalyst for all of the above.

index_5day_move:DOW.narrative: Broad-market and cyclical names have lagged over the past week as rising Treasury yields and oil prices weigh on rate-sensitive and industrial stocks more than mega-cap tech. A hot core CPI print (+0.3% m/m vs +0.2% forecast) raised the odds of a Fed hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting from ~70% to ~90%, and Iran's attacks on commercial/naval vessels in the Middle East have pushed oil higher, adding an inflation and cost headwind for industrials and consumer names that make up a larger share of the Dow than the Nasdaq.

citations.title: Global Bond Selloff Sends 10-Year Treasury Yields to Cusp of 5%

The same Middle East-driven oil spike also raises input costs disproportionately for smaller, less diversified companies.

ORCL.narrative: IMPORTANT CROSS-CURRENT: Oracle fell despite a Q1 "beat and raise" print, and separately dropped 5.4% on Sept 1 as the bond selloff punished it specifically for financing risk - Oracle has negative $23.7B free cash flow from building AI data centers, raised $43B in debt last year plus a planned $20B equity raise. Down 59% from last September's peak. This is the financing-risk mirror image of the HPE/DELL AI-capex bull case: same theme, opposite market verdict when the balance sheet is stretched. UPDATE (2026-09-14, same-day as this pull): Oracle fell another ~4.8% to a near-two-week low after expanding its 2026 restructuring plan by $700M (total charges now $2.8B) to cover layoff severance, even as Larry Ellison canceled a planned $7.5B stock sale - a move that would normally read as a bullish insider signal but was overshadowed by broader AI-stock selling and rising Fed-hike odds. Revenue still grew 30% last quarter; interest expense up 55% y/y keeps the financing-risk thesis intact.
